title: All 11 of these international organisations sit inside 4.4 km of central Geneva — and a 6 km search finds no more.
source: Source: Wikidata (query.wikidata.org/sparql), organisations within 6 km of central Geneva
axisCaption: Distance from central Geneva, kilometres — one tick per organisation
conclusion: 10 of the 11 lie within 3.4 km. Then 1.0 km of nothing, World Economic Forum at 4.4 km — and nothing at all in the last 1.6 km.
caveat: The sweep is the source's own query: Wikidata was asked for international organisations within 6 km of central Geneva, so the empty outer ring is a result and not a missing layer. Colour carries one thing here — reached by the search, or not yet — so the three categories the static sibling encodes are not on this frame. Every point is the organisation's own Wikidata coordinate, not an address, and 2 markers are nudged apart on screen to stay separately visible, so no marker may be read as a surveyed position.
alt: Map of central Geneva. A circle grows out from a marked point at central Geneva until it reaches 6 kilometres, the radius the source's own Wikidata query used, and each of 11 international organisations appears as the circle passes it. A bar under the map carries the same 0-to-6 km scale with one tick per organisation, so the shape of the distribution is readable without the map: 10 ticks are bunched between 1.8 and 3.4 km, then there is a gap of 1.0 km, then a single tick for World Economic Forum at 4.4 km, and then 1.6 km of bar with no tick at all. The nearest is European Free Trade Association at 1.8 km. The four UN-system bodies in the set are not the four nearest: they rank 3, 6, 8, 9 of 11 by distance.
